paragraphs: A risk controlling prediction set lets a model return a set of possible answers while providing a statistical guarantee about a chosen risk measure. This paper extends that idea to data arriving sequentially. Its guarantees accommodate adaptive data collection and hold simultaneously across time steps, so their validity does not depend on assessing the procedure at one predetermined moment.

The method also supports active labeling: a policy decides whether to request the true label for each incoming example. It constrains the expected proportion of requested labels to a specified budget. Predictions of risk conditional on the input information can further improve the usefulness of the resulting prediction sets.

The authors characterize optimal labeling policies and risk predictors, and connect errors in estimating them to the statistical evidence process supporting the guarantees. Experiments on simulated and real data show that practical versions of their policies achieve higher utility with fewer labels than naive labeling strategies. The contribution therefore combines sequential statistical protection with more selective use of labeling resources.
neurips-2024-active-anytime-valid-risk-c.tldr: The method builds prediction sets with risk guarantees that remain valid over time while selectively requesting labels within an expected budget.

paragraphs: Detecting hallucinations in long answers requires annotated examples, but collecting those examples is expensive and automatic annotators can be unreliable. ANAH-v2 addresses these linked problems with an iterative training process that expands the annotation dataset while improving the model responsible for labeling it. The aim is to make hallucination oversight scale beyond small, narrowly focused datasets.

The framework follows an expectation-maximization approach. Each round uses an automatic pipeline to annotate an expanded dataset, then trains an improved annotator on that data. The updated annotator becomes part of the pipeline for the next round. Dataset growth and annotator improvement are therefore connected within the same repeated procedure.

The resulting model has 7 billion parameters and, in the reported evaluations, surpasses GPT-4 and achieves leading zero-shot hallucination detection results on HaluEval and HalluQA. The authors also use it to assess other language models and help reduce hallucinations in generated answers. On HaluEval, that mitigation raises the reported Natural Language Inference metric from 25% to 37%.
neurips-2024-anah-v2-scaling-analytical-.tldr: ANAH-v2 iteratively expands hallucination annotations and improves its annotator, producing a 7-billion-parameter model with strong reported detection and mitigation results.

paragraphs: This paper examines whether the language model inside a forecasting system actually contributes to its predictions. The authors study three recent, popular approaches that apply large language models to time series. Their central method is ablation: remove or replace a component and observe whether the system loses the performance that supposedly depends on it.

Removing the language model, or substituting a basic attention layer, does not reduce forecasting performance in these studies. Results improve in most cases. The authors also find that pretrained language models do no better than models trained from scratch, fail to represent the time series' sequential dependencies, and provide no assistance in the evaluated few-shot settings.

Further experiments with time series encoders show that patching and attention structures perform similarly to the language-model-based forecasters. Together, these findings question whether the computational expense of pretrained language models is justified in the examined systems. The evidence concerns the studied methods and settings; its practical force is to identify simpler components that can account for comparable forecasting performance.
neurips-2024-are-language-models-actuall.tldr: Ablations of three forecasting methods find that removing or simplifying their language model components preserves—and often improves—performance.

paragraphs: ColJailBreak studies a safety vulnerability that spans image generation and editing. Existing adversarial prompts can be blocked once identified, motivating the authors to examine a different route: begin with an acceptable generated image and subsequently alter it to introduce unsafe content. The concern is whether protection at the initial generation stage covers the complete workflow.

The proposed system coordinates safe prompt substitution, image inpainting, and optimization guided by relationships between text and images. At a conceptual level, these components connect the initial acceptable output with a later edited result. The approach relies on the described gap between safety filtering in generation and the absence of a corresponding safety strategy in the editing models considered.

The authors evaluate their method on three datasets against two baselines and report generating unsafe content through systems involving GPT-4 and DALL·E 2. These findings expose a vulnerability in the evaluated generation-and-editing combinations. The paper's significance is its demonstration that the safety behavior of individual stages does not by itself establish the safety of their combined use.
neurips-2024-coljailbreak-collaborative-.tldr: ColJailBreak demonstrates a safety gap in evaluated image workflows by combining initially acceptable generation with subsequent unsafe editing.

paragraphs: Multimodal fusion combines complementary information from different input types. Coupled Mamba addresses the difficulty of modeling relationships both within each modality and across modalities as their internal states evolve. It uses state space models, whose changing hidden states offer a way to represent these interactions, while accounting for the parallel computation requirements that make Mamba efficient.

The architecture gives each modality its own state chain and couples those chains through their transitions. A current state depends on previous states from its own chain and neighboring chains, while the within-modality state processes retain their independence. The authors derive a global convolution kernel using historical state information to make this coupled formulation compatible with hardware-aware parallelism.

Experiments on CMU-MOSEI, CH-SIMS, and CH-SIMSV2 report F1 improvements of 0.4%, 0.9%, and 2.3%, respectively, over current leading methods. The abstract also reports 49% faster inference and 83.7% lower GPU memory use. These results support the proposed combination of richer cross-modal interaction modeling and efficient computation in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2024-coupled-mamba-enhanced-mult.tldr: Coupled Mamba connects modality-specific state chains to improve multimodal fusion while reporting faster inference and lower GPU memory use.

paragraphs: Joint detection and instance segmentation models locate objects and delineate their individual shapes. The authors observe that, early in MaskDINO's transformer decoder, detection performance trails segmentation performance. Their preliminary qualitative and quantitative experiments indicate that this imbalance negatively affects the model's eventual results, motivating an intervention at the beginning of decoding.

DI-MaskDINO adds two modules to address that imbalance. The De-Imbalance module produces a query designed to account for both tasks. Balance-Aware Tokens Optimization then uses this query to improve the initial feature tokens. The decoder receives the balance-aware query together with the optimized tokens as its attention inputs, connecting the two adjustments directly to joint prediction.

Evaluations on COCO and BDD100K report stronger performance than existing joint models. Compared with MaskDINO, the reported gains are 1.2 box AP and 0.9 mask AP. Comparisons with specialist models also show gains of 1.0 box AP over DINO and 3.0 mask AP over Mask2Former. The findings support improving early task balance as a route to better final predictions.
neurips-2024-di-maskdino-a-joint-object-.tldr: DI-MaskDINO improves joint detection and segmentation by correcting an early imbalance between the two tasks in MaskDINO's decoder.

paragraphs: Local feature matching identifies corresponding locations across images. The paper targets a recurring trade-off: convolutional approaches often match quickly, while transformer approaches tend to deliver greater accuracy. ETO introduces a transformer architecture intended to retain competitive matching quality while reducing the time required to produce those correspondences.

Its main design organizes matching around multiple homography hypotheses, using several candidate geometric mappings to approximate real-world correspondence. It then employs cross-attention in one direction to accelerate refinement. These two choices address the structure of the matching problem and the cost of refining matches, respectively, rather than treating efficiency as a separate step after prediction.

On YFCC100M, the authors report accuracy competitive with LoFTR and inference four times as fast, with speed also exceeding the CNN-based methods considered. Additional evaluations on Megadepth, ScanNet, and HPatches support the method's effectiveness. The result matters because it shows an evaluated transformer matcher can substantially improve speed without giving up competitive accuracy, creating potential benefits for applications that depend on image correspondences.
neurips-2024-eto-efficient-transformer-b.tldr: ETO uses multiple geometric mapping hypotheses and one-way cross-attention to achieve competitive feature matching with substantially faster inference.

paragraphs: Training data often contain incorrect labels, sets of possible labels, or examples without labels. Methods designed separately for each situation become difficult to combine when several kinds of uncertainty occur together. Imprecise Label Learning, or ILL, provides a shared framework for representing and learning from these different forms of incomplete supervision.

ILL treats the precise labels as hidden variables and uses expectation-maximization to model the available label information. Instead of choosing an estimated correct label for each example, it accounts for the distribution over possible labelings supported by that information. This preserves uncertainty within the learning formulation rather than resolving it prematurely into a single training target.

The authors derive closed-form objectives for partial-label, semi-supervised, and noisy-label learning, as well as mixtures of these settings. They report that ILL outperforms existing specialized techniques across the challenging settings examined. The contribution is therefore both organizational and practical: one probabilistic formulation handles several labeling configurations while delivering strong reported results where precise annotations are costly or difficult to obtain.
neurips-2024-imprecise-label-learning-a-.tldr: ILL unifies learning from noisy, partial, and missing labels by modeling distributions over possible true labels with expectation-maximization.

paragraphs: Recognizing material states involves distinguishing conditions such as wetness, burning, or infection across image regions. These states can vary gradually and appear in scattered patches, making precise manual annotation difficult. Synthetic scenes provide accurate labels at scale, but the paper identifies their limited real-world diversity as an obstacle to learning this task.

The proposed approach automatically extracts patterns from natural images and uses them to generate materials for synthetic scenes. This unsupervised process brings real visual variation into data that retain the annotation precision of synthetic generation. The authors also introduce a benchmark spanning domains including food, soils, construction, plants, and liquids, with annotations for both partial material similarity and exact material-state matches.

Leading foundation models struggle on the benchmark, while networks trained with the infused synthetic data perform significantly better on this and related tasks. The findings support enriching synthetic materials with patterns drawn from real images. Alongside the dataset, code, and trained model, the authors release 300,000 textures and rendering materials to support further dataset creation.
neurips-2024-infusing-synthetic-data-wit.tldr: The paper enriches synthetic materials with automatically extracted natural patterns and reports improved segmentation of material states on a new benchmark.

paragraphs: An agent trained with simulated teammates may struggle with people whose strategies differ from those simulations. GAMMA addresses this diversity problem by learning a generative model of partners. Its goal is to prepare a cooperating agent for zero-shot coordination with humans by exposing it to a broader range of partner behaviors during training.

The partner model learns a latent representation that can be interpreted as encoding differences in strategy, intention, experience, or style. Sampling this representation produces different training partners. The model can learn from interaction data involving either humans or neural policies, allowing the same approach to use human datasets or populations of simulated agents.

In the cooperative cooking game Overcooked, evaluations with real human teammates show consistent performance improvements using either source of training data. The authors also introduce posterior sampling that favors behaviors supported by human observations. This provides an additional way to improve performance using only a small amount of costly human interaction data, connecting broad simulated partner diversity with targeted information about actual people.
neurips-2024-learning-to-cooperate-with-.tldr: GAMMA generates diverse training partners from a learned latent model and improves coordination with real humans in Overcooked.

paragraphs: This paper studies lossy compression when reconstructed outputs follow a different distribution from the original source. Its formulation uses logarithmic loss and is motivated by settings combining compression with retrieval or involving distribution changes caused by processing. It extends minimum entropy coupling by adding a bottleneck that controls how much randomness the relationship between source and reconstruction can contain.

The authors divide the resulting problem into two parts. The encoder solves Entropy-Bounded Information Maximization, while the decoder solves a minimum entropy coupling problem. This separation makes the respective responsibilities explicit. For the encoder problem, they develop a greedy algorithm with a performance guarantee and analyze optimal solutions near functional mappings.

Experiments use Markov Coding Games under communication rate limits. In these games, an agent conveys a compressed message through actions within a Markov decision process. The results illustrate how changing the compression rate affects both task rewards and the receiver's accuracy, and show effectiveness relative to a conventional compression baseline. The framework thus connects compression structure with the competing demands of acting and communicating.
neurips-2024-minimum-entropy-coupling-wi.tldr: MEC-B adds a bottleneck to minimum entropy coupling, separating encoder and decoder optimization for compression with differing source and reconstruction distributions.

paragraphs: Off-dynamics reinforcement learning asks whether an agent can transfer a policy between environments whose dynamics differ. A policy's actions may have different consequences in the target environment, so successful transfer requires adapting to that mismatch. ODRL addresses the lack of a common benchmark for comparing methods designed to handle this problem.

The benchmark includes four settings covering online and offline combinations for source and target domains. It supplies diverse tasks and a broad range of dynamics shifts, allowing evaluation across several forms of adaptation rather than one narrowly defined change. Recent algorithms and additional baselines are brought together in a unified framework with single-file implementations.

Extensive benchmarking finds that no evaluated method has an advantage across all the dynamics shifts examined. This result makes the variety of benchmark conditions central to its contribution: performance under one type of mismatch does not establish superiority across the others. ODRL provides a shared basis for studying those differences and comparing future methods under consistently defined source and target conditions.
neurips-2024-odrl-a-benchmark-for-off-dy.tldr: ODRL benchmarks policy transfer across changing environment dynamics and finds no evaluated method consistently dominates across all tested shifts.

paragraphs: Researchers have proposed describing neural network training trajectories with fractal geometry to help explain generalization. In particular, dimensions estimated through persistent homology have been suggested as measures associated with the generalization gap. This paper empirically tests how well those measures behave, using detailed statistical analysis to examine the relationships behind their apparent predictive value.

The analysis finds that changes in hyperparameters confound observed correlations between topological measures and generalization. This matters because a correlation can reflect the influence of another changing factor rather than a direct relationship between the quantities being compared. The authors also find that fractal dimension fails to predict generalization for models trained from poor initializations.

A further observation is that these topological measures exhibit model-wise double descent. Taken together, the results identify complications in using trajectory geometry as a generalization measure. The paper provides evidence for investigating the causal relationships among fractal structure, topology, and optimization more carefully, rather than treating an observed correlation as a sufficient explanation of a network's ability to generalize.
neurips-2024-on-the-limitations-of-fract.tldr: An empirical statistical study finds confounding and prediction failures in fractal-dimension measures proposed to explain neural network generalization.

paragraphs: Procedure learning identifies the key steps of a task and their logical order from multiple videos. Existing approaches often compare frames directly or assume video pairs can be aligned monotonically in time. OPEL instead treats frames as samples from unknown distributions and uses optimal transport to compare them, relaxing those alignment assumptions.

The method adds two forms of regularization to this transport problem. One favors correspondence between frames that are similar in their learned representations and close in time. The other uses KL divergence with an exponentially decaying prior to smooth the alignment while preserving guidance from both the unregularized transport solution and temporal information.

OPEL reports substantial improvements on first-person and third-person procedure-learning benchmarks. On EgoProceL, the average improvements over the current leading method are 22.4% in intersection over union and 26.9% in F1. Across ProCeL and CrossTask, the reported average F1 improvement is 46.2%. These results support combining a more flexible distributional alignment with explicit preferences for visual similarity and temporal coherence.
neurips-2024-opel-optimal-transport-guid.tldr: OPEL uses regularized optimal transport to align task videos more flexibly and improves procedure learning on egocentric and third-person benchmarks.

paragraphs: Fair-range clustering adds representation requirements to the selection of cluster facilities. Each data point carries one or more demographic labels, and the selected facilities must meet lower and upper bounds for each label. The fairness requirement therefore concerns which facilities are opened and how their labels are represented, alongside the usual clustering objective.

The paper studies both k-median and k-means in Euclidean spaces. It provides approximation algorithms with a factor of one plus epsilon, meaning their objective values can approach the optimum according to the chosen approximation tolerance. Their running times are fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the number of opened facilities and the number of demographic labels.

These are the first parameterized approximation schemes for the stated Euclidean problems. They improve on previously available constant-factor approximation guarantees. The contribution is a theoretical improvement in achievable solution quality under demographic representation constraints, with computational tractability expressed through the two specified parameters. This framing ties the guarantee to the structure of the clustering problem rather than claiming unrestricted computational efficiency.
neurips-2024-parameterized-approximation.tldr: The paper gives the first parameterized approximation schemes for Euclidean fair-range k-median and k-means under demographic facility-selection constraints.

paragraphs: ReMI evaluates whether language models can reason using multiple images. The paper treats this as an emerging capability that needs dedicated assessment as models become more capable. Its contribution is a dataset designed to reveal what models can infer from collections of images and where their reasoning still falls short.

The dataset covers mathematics, physics, logic, code, tables and charts, and spatial and temporal reasoning. It also spans varied characteristics of multi-image scenarios. This breadth allows the evaluation to examine several kinds of reasoning within the same resource, making it possible to compare models' strengths and weaknesses across different task categories.

Benchmarking several leading language models reveals a substantial gap from human-level proficiency. The accompanying analysis identifies reasoning types that current models can handle and areas where improvement is needed. ReMI therefore contributes both a common evaluation resource and evidence that multi-image reasoning remains challenging for the evaluated systems. Its proposed role in future development is to help assess progress toward more capable real-world multi-image understanding.
neurips-2024-remi-a-dataset-for-reasonin.tldr: ReMI tests reasoning across multiple images and reveals a substantial performance gap between evaluated language models and humans.

paragraphs: Riemannian neural networks represent features in curved geometric spaces, creating a need for classification methods suited to those spaces. Existing extensions of multinomial logistic regression often depend heavily on particular geometric properties. RMLR proposes a broader framework that requires fewer geometric properties, making the same general classification design applicable to a wider range of geometries.

The authors demonstrate the framework on symmetric positive definite matrices and on rotation matrices. For the former, they construct five families of classifiers using five types of power-deformed metrics. For rotations, they introduce a Lie-group version of multinomial logistic regression based on a bi-invariant metric. These examples show how the framework supports distinct geometric settings.

Experiments with different Riemannian backbone networks validate the framework's effectiveness. The significance is the ability to design classification layers without tying the entire approach to one narrowly specified geometry. Its broad applicability follows from the reduced geometric requirements, while the concrete constructions and experiments establish working instances on the two manifold types studied.
neurips-2024-rmlr-extending-multinomial-.tldr: RMLR generalizes multinomial logistic regression across geometric spaces and demonstrates effective classifiers for positive definite matrices and rotations.

paragraphs: S²FT aims to combine fine-tuning quality, training efficiency, and scalable serving. It selects a small number of attention heads and feedforward channels in each transformer block. Coordinated permutations of the connected weight matrices group the selected parameters into dense submatrices, which are then updated in place. Sparse selection thus remains compatible with dense computation.

Theoretical analysis and experiments support reduced forgetting and simpler optimization. The reported average improvements over LoRA are 4.6% for commonsense reasoning and 1.3% for arithmetic reasoning. After instruction tuning, S²FT also surpasses full fine-tuning by 11.5% when generalizing across the evaluated domains, connecting selective parameter updates with stronger reported transfer.

A partial backpropagation algorithm reduces training memory use by up to threefold and improves latency by 1.5–2.7 times relative to full fine-tuning. Both measures improve by an average of 10% over LoRA. The authors further show that updates can be separated into adapters, supporting fusion, switching, and parallel serving of multiple fine-tuned models. The design therefore addresses both adaptation and deployment costs.
neurips-2024-s-2-ft-efficient-scalable-a.tldr: S²FT updates selected heads and channels as dense parameter blocks, reporting improved fine-tuning performance, efficiency, and support for scalable serving.

paragraphs: SemCoder addresses the gap between producing plausible code text and understanding what code does during execution. The authors train a code language model to reason about overall functionality, the effects of individual statements, and input-output behavior. Their monologue reasoning approach uses natural-language explanations resembling a programmer talking through a debugging problem.

Training begins with PyX, a Python corpus containing executable samples, functional descriptions, and test cases. The model learns both code generation and reasoning about properties, constraints, and execution behavior. This connects static source text with dynamic program states and gives the training process several complementary views of program semantics.

The resulting 6.7-billion-parameter model achieves 79.3% on HumanEval, 63.6% on CRUXEval-I, and 63.9% on CRUXEval-O, exceeding the reported GPT-3.5-turbo scores on those tasks. A comparison with concrete scratchpad reasoning finds that monologue reasoning integrates multiple semantic dimensions more smoothly. The authors also demonstrate potential benefits for debugging and self-refinement, suggesting that learned execution understanding can support improvements beyond initial code generation.
neurips-2024-semcoder-training-code-lang.tldr: SemCoder trains code models to explain program behavior in natural language, improving reported code generation and execution reasoning performance.

paragraphs: This paper compares continuous-time gradient methods in a two-layer linear network trained with square loss. Its focus is the rank of a parameter matrix, which describes how many independent directions that matrix retains. The analysis reveals different behavior for ordinary gradient descent and stochastic gradient descent with label noise.

Under the studied formulation, gradient descent preserves the rank present at initialization, whereas label-noise stochastic gradient descent reduces rank regardless of initialization. The authors establish the rank deficiency by examining how the determinant of a parameter matrix changes over time. This gives a concrete mathematical route for tracking the loss of independent parameter directions.

To explain the mechanism further, they derive a stochastic differential equation for the matrix's eigenvalues. It reveals a repulsive interaction between eigenvalues that the authors identify as a key regularizing mechanism inducing rank deficiency. Experiments also illustrate the phenomenon beyond linear networks and regression. Those experiments broaden the supporting evidence, while the stated theoretical analysis remains centered on continuous-time methods for the two-layer linear setting.
neurips-2024-sgd-vs-gd-rank-deficiency-i.tldr: For continuous-time training of two-layer linear networks, the paper shows that label-noise SGD reduces parameter rank while GD preserves its initial rank.

paragraphs: Neural ordinary differential equations learn transformations through continuous dynamics, but training can require many solver evaluations and unstable gradient estimates. This paper adapts flow matching to train them for deterministic mappings between paired inputs and outputs. The dynamics are trained directly against a target velocity field, avoiding trajectory simulation during training.

Applying flow matching directly to paired data creates a specific difficulty: trajectories can cross, producing an ill-defined flow that fails to preserve the intended input-output pairings. The authors address this by learning an embedding space for the pairs jointly with the dynamics. Flow matching takes place in that space, where the learned representation supports a valid flow that is easier to learn.

Experiments cover both regression and classification. The proposed method outperforms existing neural ODE approaches while requiring significantly fewer function evaluations. Its contribution is therefore more than a faster training objective: it adapts that objective to the pairing constraints of supervised learning, using learned representations to address a failure that can arise when directly transferring flow matching from generative settings.
neurips-2024-simulation-free-training-of.tldr: The method jointly learns embeddings and flow-matched dynamics to train neural ODEs on paired data without simulating trajectories during training.

paragraphs: Confocal fluorescence microscopy faces a tension between image quality and light exposure. Reducing exposure can lessen specimen damage but also degrade the images. Single-image super-resolution offers a way to improve lower-resolution images computationally, yet its development for this microscopy setting has been constrained partly by the shortage of publicly available data.

SR-CACO-2 supplies paired low- and high-resolution images of the human Caco-2 epithelial cell line. It contains 2,200 unique images captured at four resolutions with three fluorescent markers, organized into 9,937 patches for experiments. The dataset supports evaluation at twofold, fourfold, and eightfold upscaling, providing several levels of reconstruction difficulty within the same resource.

The authors benchmark 16 leading methods representing major super-resolution families. These methods have limited success recovering high-resolution textures, establishing the dataset as a challenging test of microscopy image reconstruction. The release includes the dataset, code, and pretrained weights, with the data available under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Its contribution is both a shared experimental resource and evidence of remaining texture-reconstruction difficulties in the evaluated methods.
neurips-2024-sr-caco-2-a-dataset-for-con.tldr: SR-CACO-2 provides paired microscopy images for super-resolution and shows that 16 evaluated methods struggle to reconstruct high-resolution textures.

paragraphs: A foundation model may need to offer several useful responses to accommodate different user preferences. Producing those alternatives while preserving accuracy is difficult, particularly with greedy sampling. Synthesize-Partition-Adapt, or SPA, addresses this problem by using synthetic data to train multiple adaptations that emphasize different aspects of the available examples.

The framework uses signals from data attribution methods, including influence functions, to divide synthetic data into subsets. Each subset targets distinct aspects of the data, and a separate model adaptation is optimized for it. Diversity is therefore encouraged through the organization of training data and the resulting adaptations, giving the models different learned emphases.

Experiments on HumanEval and MBPP for code generation, together with several natural-language-understanding tasks, show more diverse responses while maintaining high quality. The results support SPA as a way to elicit useful variation from foundation models using abundant synthetic examples. Its potential value lies in offering a broader selection of responses without requiring the reported gains in diversity to come at the expense of response quality.
neurips-2024-synthesize-partition-then-a.tldr: SPA partitions synthetic data using attribution signals and trains specialized adaptations that produce more diverse, high-quality responses.

paragraphs: Layer width strongly affects a neural network's computational cost, yet it is often chosen empirically. This paper investigates whether training behavior can indicate when a layer is sufficiently wide. Its proposed signal is the variance of weight norms across channels: how unevenly the magnitudes of different channels' weights are distributed.

The starting intuition is that channels with larger weights receive larger gradients, allowing initially similar channels to become increasingly unequal. Experiments across different data modalities and architectures reveal distinct patterns for wide and narrow layers. The authors use those patterns to identify three stages of training and provide evidence explaining the behavior in each stage.

They then propose adjusting layer widths according to the observed pattern. In their CNN experiments, this allows conventional width choices to be revised in ways that reduce parameter counts while improving performance. The findings suggest that variation in channel weight magnitudes can provide useful feedback for allocating capacity across layers. The claim is an empirically supported indicator and adjustment strategy, rather than a universal prescription for every network.
neurips-2024-unveiling-the-matthew-effec.tldr: Patterns in channel weight-norm variance indicate layer-width sufficiency and guide CNN width changes that reduce parameters while improving reported performance.

paragraphs: Adversarial perturbations can look like random noise yet carry information associated with particular classes. One piece of evidence is perturbation learning: classifiers trained on adversarial examples and their incorrect labels can still generalize to correctly labeled test data. This paper develops a theoretical explanation for that counterintuitive result.

The analysis assumes wide two-layer networks and holds for any data distribution within that setting. The authors prove that adversarial perturbations contain enough class-specific information for networks to generalize from them. This gives a mathematical foundation for the hypothesis that perturbations encode learnable features, even when their visual appearance suggests unstructured noise.

The paper further shows that classifiers trained on the mislabeled adversarial examples produce predictions coinciding with those of classifiers trained on correctly labeled clean samples. This prediction-level correspondence strengthens the explanation of why perturbation learning can succeed. The breadth over data distributions is significant, while the wide two-layer network assumption defines the stated theoretical scope. The result supports a structured-information view of adversarial perturbations in that setting.
neurips-2024-wide-two-layer-networks-can.tldr: For wide two-layer networks, the paper proves that adversarial perturbations contain sufficient class information to explain successful learning from mislabeled adversarial examples.
